label: 6.8 Indicator and Dummy Variables — mastery test

items.stem: A variable records teaching format: classroom, online or blended. This variable is:
items.explanation: The values name groups rather than measure a numerical amount.

items.stem: With an intercept and K categories, the usual number of indicator variables is:
items.explanation: One category is kept as the reference, leaving K−1 indicators.

items.stem: In a model with an intercept and K−1 indicators, the intercept represents:
options: The mean of all groups in every setting
The reference-group mean when other regressors are zero
The slope of the first group
items.explanation: All included indicators are zero for the reference group, so its baseline is the intercept.

items.stem: A fitted model is ŷ=30+5D, where D=1 for group B and 0 for group A. Find the fitted value for group B.
items.explanation: Set D=1: 30+5=35. The indicator adds five to the reference baseline.
items.check: Substitute D=1; the fitted value must be five above group A's 30.

items.stem: The dummy-variable trap with an intercept and all K category indicators is caused by:
items.explanation: The K indicators sum to the intercept column, so the columns are linearly dependent.

items.stem: A dummy variable without an interaction with x primarily allows:
items.explanation: The dummy adds a constant shift; a slope difference needs an interaction.

items.stem: There are five regions and the regression includes an intercept. How many region indicators are used?
items.explanation: Use K−1=5−1=4 indicators and omit one reference region.
items.check: One of five regions is the reference; four contrasts remain.

items.stem: For ŷ=12+2x+4D, calculate the fitted value for group B (D=1) at x=3.
items.explanation: 12+2(3)+4=22. Substitute x and D separately before adding.
items.check: The reference prediction is 18; group B is four higher, giving 22.

items.stem: In y=β₀+β₁x+β₂D+β₃xD+u, the slope for D=1 is:
items.explanation: Set D=1 and collect the coefficient of x: β₁+β₃.

items.stem: Which statements are correct? A. K−1 indicators are used with an intercept. B. The omitted category is the reference. C. All K indicators plus an intercept are full rank. D. A dummy coefficient is a contrast with the reference.
items.explanation: A, B and D are true. The intercept equals the sum of all K indicators, so C is false.
statements: K−1 indicators are used with an intercept
The omitted category is the reference
All K indicators plus an intercept are full rank
A dummy coefficient is a contrast with the reference

A.why: K−1 contrasts avoid the intercept dependence.

B.why: The omitted category is represented by all included indicators being zero.

C.why: The K indicators sum exactly to the intercept column.

D.why: The coefficient measures the conditional difference from the baseline.

items.check: A true; B true; C false; D true.

items.stem: A regression has n=50 observations and estimates an intercept, three numerical slopes and four category indicators. Find residual degrees of freedom.
items.explanation: There are 1+3+4=8 coefficients. Residual df=50−8=42.

items.stem: To test whether four group-specific intercepts are equal in a model with a common slope, the null hypothesis is:
options: All three included dummy coefficients equal zero
items.explanation: With one reference group, equality of four intercepts means all three group contrasts are zero.

items.stem: Season has four categories and the model includes an intercept. The usual seasonal coding uses:
items.explanation: One season is the reference, so three indicators represent the remaining seasons.

items.stem: If the reference category is changed in a correctly specified group-means model, the fitted values:
items.explanation: Changing the baseline re-expresses the same group means and contrasts; predictions are unchanged.

items.stem: Which term allows the slope with respect to x to differ for group B?
items.explanation: The interaction xD changes the coefficient of x when D switches from zero to one.

items.stem: For y=8+3x+2D−xD, calculate the slope for D=1.
items.explanation: For group B, set D=1; the coefficient of x becomes 3−1=2, which is the group B slope.
items.check: Collect x terms after setting D=1: (3−1)x, so the slope is 2.

items.stem: A model compares two groups using an intercept, x, D and xD. Which statements are correct? A. β₂ measures the intercept difference. B. β₃ measures the slope difference. C. β₂=β₃=0 gives identical fitted lines. D. β₃ alone tests equality of both lines.
items.explanation: A, B and C are true. D is false because equality of lines requires both intercept and slope differences to be zero.
statements: β₃ alone tests equality of both lines

A.why: The D term shifts the intercept for group B.

B.why: The xD term changes the coefficient of x.

C.why: Both group-specific intercept and slope then coincide.

D.why: A slope-only restriction does not test the intercept difference.

items.check: A true; B true; C true; D false.

items.stem: A study has n=80, an intercept, two numerical predictors and five indicators for six categories. Find residual degrees of freedom.
items.explanation: There are 1+2+5=8 coefficients, so residual df=80−8=72.
items.check: Six categories require five indicators; total p=8, so 80−8=72.

items.stem: To test whether seasonal effects are jointly absent when there are four seasons and one reference season, the number of restrictions is:
items.explanation: There are three seasonal contrast coefficients; the joint null sets all three to zero.

items.stem: A researcher includes an intercept and all four mutually exclusive region indicators. Which correction preserves an intercept interpretation and full column rank?
options: Delete one region indicator and use it as reference
items.explanation: Dropping one indicator makes that category the reference and removes the exact linear dependence.
